title: My little first-person roguelite: three generated valleys, one sword and a boss (working title: RogueLittle)
author: droid_man_
selftext:
I'm a hobby dev making a small first-person roguelite in Godot (first-look devlog: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SmswtobcASg](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SmswtobcASg)). Here's honestly how I use AI on it, since that's what this sub is about.

**Design first.** Before writing any code, I split the design into a modular design document: 17 short files, one per system, plus a file of "data contracts" saying what each system may know about the others. That made it much easier to ask for one system at a time without everything leaking into everything else.

**Code.** In the early sessions I built things myself in the Godot editor, with Claude Code explaining each step. For the bigger systems later on, like spawning, objectives, the boss, saving and menus, I let it write more of the code while I designed, play-tested every change and asked for fixes. Every tuning value is exposed in the inspector, so I can adjust things live while playing.

**What worked:**

* Prototyping a look before touching the game, with quick renders in Python first.
* The procedural pieces: a Townscaper-style grid for the cliff, and sound effects and music synthesized in code (no AI audio model).
* Sword cuts reworked around a real arm model, so the wrist stays natural.

**What didn't:**

* A whole day of generating "natural" rocks in code. Every attempt came out as pillars, boxes or blobs. The fix was to step back to a simple grid of pieces, and to model real rocks in Blender later.
* Pacing. It's easy to add systems faster than you can play-test them.

**Other AI bits:**

* The concept images for the enemies are AI-generated references, used only as targets for modelling them by hand in Blender.
* The devlog narration is a local TTS voice (Kokoro).
* The in-game models are CC0 (Quaternius) and placeholder shapes.

Happy to answer questions about any of it.

comments.author: Disastrous-Gain5870
comments.body: Why use AI for a voice in your dev log? I don’t understand why you would ever do that. It just makes it even more non personal. You’d be better off with no voice at all.
